Questions & troubleshooting

PDF to Word Questions, Answers & Troubleshooting

Straight answers to the questions people ask before and after converting a PDF to Word: why a conversion fails or looks wrong, what OCR is for, what Word and Google Docs can do on their own, whether you need Adobe, and how to keep your files safe.

First, which kind of PDF do you have?

Most answers on this page depend on what is inside your PDF. Open it in any PDF reader and look for these signs:

  • A text-based PDF was exported from Word, Google Docs or another program. You can select a word and copy it. It converts the most cleanly.
  • A scanned or image-only PDF came from a scanner, a copier or phone photos. Clicking the text selects nothing, or selects the whole page as one picture. It needs OCR (text recognition) to become editable text.
  • A complex-layout PDF has several columns, text boxes, forms or wide tables. It converts, but expect to tidy up the layout in Word.
  • A protected or damaged PDF asks for a password when you open it, or shows an error or blank pages in your reader. It has to be fixed or unlocked before any converter can read it.

General PDF to Word questions

Is a PDF a Word document? What is the difference?

No. A PDF records where every letter, line and picture sits on a fixed page, so it looks the same everywhere but is not meant to be edited. A Word document stores flowing text: paragraphs, headings, tables and styles that rewrap when you edit them.

That is why "converting" a PDF is not a simple rename. The converter has to guess which pieces of text form a paragraph, which lines form a table and which text is a heading, then rebuild them as Word structures. Simple pages rebuild well; elaborate layouts need more guessing.

What is the difference between DOC and DOCX?

DOC is the older Word format used up to Word 2003. DOCX is the current format, introduced with Word 2007, and it is what Word, Google Docs, LibreOffice and Pages open by default. PDF to Word converters, including ours, normally produce DOCX. Choose DOC only if someone specifically asks for it, by opening the DOCX in Word and saving a copy as "Word 97-2003 Document".

Can every PDF be converted to Word?

Most can, but not all. A PDF that needs a password to open can't be read until its owner removes the password. A damaged file may not open at all. A page made only of drawings or a single picture comes back as a picture, unless the converter reads it with OCR. And every online service has size and page limits: here, 25 MB per file and 20 pages on a free account (200 on Pro).

Does a PDF keep its pictures when converted to Word?

Usually, yes: photos, logos and charts are placed in the Word file as pictures you can move or resize. What you can't edit is any text that is part of a picture, such as words inside a chart or a screenshot. That text stays part of the image. On fully scanned pages, OCR reads the text from the page image instead.

Can I turn a PDF back into the original Word file?

Not exactly. Once a document is saved as PDF, the original Word structure (styles, tracked changes, comments, section settings) is not stored in the PDF. A converter rebuilds a new Word document that looks as close as possible to the PDF. If the original .docx still exists, on your computer, in your email or with the person who sent the PDF, that file will always be better than any conversion.

Free conversion: what to expect

Can I convert a PDF to Word for free?

Yes, but "free" almost always comes with conditions, so check them before you upload. Things worth comparing between free converters:

  • How many files or pages you can convert, and how often.
  • Whether scanned PDFs (OCR) are included or reserved for paid plans.
  • Whether you need an account, and whether the result carries a watermark.
  • How long your files stay on the service, written in its privacy policy.

On PDF2Wordly, sign-in is required. A free account converts 1 PDF every 24 hours on the website, up to 20 pages and 25 MB, with OCR for up to 20 scanned pages. Pro ($4.99/month) raises this to 100 files per day and 200 pages per file (scanned PDFs: up to 50). Files are deleted within 1 hour at most.

What is the most accurate way to convert a PDF to Word?

Start from the cleanest source you can get. In order:

  1. Ask for the original Word file. Nothing beats it.
  2. Convert the PDF exported directly from the program, not a printed-and-scanned copy.
  3. For a scan, use a straight, sharp scan at about 300 DPI so OCR has clear letters to read.
  4. Check the result: tables, page breaks, numbers and names are where errors hide.

No converter reproduces every PDF identically, because the PDF doesn't store the document's original structure.

Converting without Adobe

Do you need Adobe Acrobat to convert a PDF to Word?

No. PDF is an open file format, not something only Adobe software can read. Adobe offers its own conversion tools, but you can also:

  • open the PDF in Microsoft Word on a computer, which converts it into an editable copy (see what Word can do);
  • open it with Google Docs from Google Drive, mainly to get the text out (see what Google Docs keeps);
  • use an online PDF to Word converter in any browser, such as ours.

Which one is right depends on your file. Adobe's own plans and features change over time, so check Adobe's website for what its current tools include.

Do I need an Adobe account to convert a PDF?

Not for tools that aren't made by Adobe. Be careful not to confuse two different things, though: not needing an Adobe account doesn't mean a tool needs no account at all. Many converters ask you to sign in, and PDF2Wordly does: you need a PDF2Wordly account (Google or email) to convert, but no Adobe account or Adobe software.

How can I convert a PDF to Word on a Mac without Adobe?

Use an online converter in Safari, Chrome or Firefox, then open the .docx in Word, Pages or Google Docs. Preview, the PDF viewer built into macOS, lets you copy text out of a text-based PDF, which is fine for a few paragraphs but loses the layout. Step-by-step instructions for each device are in PDF to Word on Mac, iPhone and Android.

Why conversions go wrong, and how to fix them

Find the symptom closest to yours. A symptom can have more than one cause, so start with the quickest check.

Why won't my PDF convert to Word at all?

When a converter refuses a file or stops partway, the cause is usually one of these:

  • The PDF needs a password to open. No converter can read an encrypted file without it. See damaged or password-protected PDFs.
  • The file isn't really a PDF, for example a picture or Word file renamed to .pdf. Many converters, including ours, check the file's content, not just its name.
  • The file is damaged or was only partly downloaded. Download it again and check that it opens in a PDF reader.
  • The file is over a limit: size, pages, scanned pages or processing time. Split it into parts.

For the specific messages shown by PDF2Wordly (upload, sign-in and daily-limit messages), see PDF to Word not working.

Why is my PDF not converting to Word correctly?

Because a PDF doesn't say what is a paragraph, a heading or a table; it only says where each piece of text is drawn. Microsoft describes the same problem for Word's own PDF import: a table in a PDF is stored as lines with no link to the text inside the cells, so the converter has to infer the structure with rules (Microsoft Support: Opening PDFs in Word). The more a page relies on precise positioning, such as columns, text boxes, forms and decorative layouts, the more the rebuilt Word document can differ.

Results are usually good for mostly-text documents like letters, reports and contracts, and need more checking for brochures, forms and magazine-style pages.

Why is my converted Word document blank?

If the file has the right number of pages but they look empty, try these in order:

  1. Press Ctrl+A (Cmd+A on a Mac). If highlighted text appears, it is there but colored white or very light: change the font color.
  2. In Word, choose View, then Print Layout. Some views hide pictures and text boxes.
  3. Go back to the PDF and try to select its text. If nothing is selectable, the pages are images; a converter without OCR may produce empty or picture-only pages. Use a converter with OCR.
  4. If the PDF itself looks blank in some readers, the file may be damaged or depend on features only one reader supports. Re-save it from the reader that shows it correctly, then convert that copy.

Why can't I edit the text in my converted Word document?

  • The page is a picture. Click the text: if a frame with resize handles appears around the whole block, it is an image, not text. This happens when a scanned page is converted without OCR. Convert it again with OCR; our scanned PDF to Word page explains how it works.
  • Word opened it in Protected View. Files from the internet open read-only until you click "Enable Editing" in the yellow bar.
  • Editing is restricted in the document. In Word, check Review, then Restrict Editing.
  • The text sits in text boxes. It is editable, but you have to click inside each box. You can copy the text out of the boxes into normal paragraphs.

Why is text missing after PDF to Word conversion?

Text can be part of a PDF without being part of the page content a converter reads:

  • Comments, sticky notes and filled-in form fields are stored as separate layers and are often skipped. In your PDF reader, flatten the form or print to a new PDF first, then convert that copy.
  • Hidden layers in technical drawings or brochures may not be converted. Turn on the layers you need in your reader, then print to a new PDF.
  • Text inside pictures stays part of the picture on normal pages.
  • Parts of a scan the OCR couldn't read, such as handwriting or faint stamps, may be left out. Our converter keeps a page it can't read as an image with a short note instead of dropping it.

Why are characters wrong or unreadable after conversion?

Copy a sentence from the PDF and paste it into Notepad (Windows) or TextEdit (Mac):

  • If the pasted text is gibberish too, the PDF's own text layer is broken: the fonts inside it don't record which letter each shape is. Every converter that reads that text layer gets the same gibberish. Ask the sender for a new export, or treat the file like a scan so the letters are read from the page image with OCR.
  • If the pasted text is fine, the problem is in the conversion. For a scan, a sharper, straighter scan at about 300 DPI helps OCR; for text documents, check that the fonts used in the result are installed on your computer.

What should I do if my PDF is damaged or password-protected?

Damaged: download the file again from its source, since many "damaged" files are just incomplete downloads. If it opens in at least one PDF reader, use that reader's Print to PDF or Save As to write a fresh copy, and convert the copy.

Password-protected: if the PDF asks for a password to open, only someone who has the password can remove it. Unlock it in your PDF reader, save an unprotected copy, then convert. If you don't have the password, ask the person or organization that created the file. Some PDFs open without a password but restrict editing or copying; respect those restrictions unless you are the owner or have permission. More details: password-protected PDF to Word.

Why do my PDFs open in Word automatically?

Word has been set as the default app for PDF files, so double-clicking a PDF makes Word convert a copy of it. To change it:

  • Windows: right-click a PDF, choose Open with, then Choose another app. Pick your PDF reader and tick "Always use this app".
  • Mac: select a PDF in Finder, choose File, then Get Info. Under "Open with", pick Preview or your PDF reader and click Change All.
  • Android: open Settings, then Apps, find the app that opens your PDFs and clear its default settings. The menu names vary by phone; the next PDF you open will let you pick an app.

Formatting and layout

Why does my Word document look different from the PDF?

Three things change most often:

  • Fonts: a PDF can carry its fonts inside the file, but Word uses the fonts installed on your computer. If one is missing, Word substitutes a similar font, and line breaks shift.
  • Alignment and spacing: text that was placed line by line in the PDF becomes paragraphs or text boxes in Word, so justified text, indents and spacing can change when the paragraph rewraps.
  • Page flow: once text can move, a slightly longer line pushes content to the next page.

How to keep as much as possible, and what to check afterwards, is covered in PDF to Word without losing formatting.

Which parts of a PDF are hardest to convert?

Microsoft's list for Word's own PDF import gives a good idea of what any converter struggles with: tables with cell spacing, page colors and borders, tracked changes, frames, footnotes that span pages, endnotes, audio and video, PDF bookmarks, tags and comments, and font effects like glow or shadow (source).

Hyperlinks, headers and footers depend on how the PDF was made: a link is only kept if the PDF stores it as a link, not just as blue underlined text. After converting, click a few links and check the first and last pages. For tables in invoices and reports, see PDF tables to Word.

Scanned PDFs and OCR

How can I tell if my PDF needs OCR?

Open it and try to select one word. If you can highlight single words and copy them, the page has real text and doesn't need OCR. If nothing is selected, or the whole page is selected like a photo, the page is an image and needs OCR (optical character recognition), which reads the letters from the picture and turns them into text.

This test is a good guide, not a guarantee. Some scans already carry a hidden OCR text layer of poor quality, and one PDF can mix text pages and scanned pages. Our converter checks every page on its own and runs OCR only where it is needed; the scanned PDF to Word guide explains the process, the languages and tips for a cleaner scan.

Can I convert a photo of a document to Word?

Yes, once it is inside a PDF: our converter accepts PDF files only, not JPG or PNG. Your phone's document scanner (in the Files app on iPhone, or Google Drive on Android) saves photos as a PDF and also straightens and crops them, which helps OCR. Then convert that PDF like any scan.

Phones and computers

Converting works the same in any modern browser on Windows, Mac, Android, iPhone and iPad; the step-by-step PDF to Word guide covers each method. The questions below are about what happens around the conversion.

Where is my converted Word file after I download it?

  • Android: in the Downloads folder. Open the Files app (or "Files by Google") and choose Downloads, or open your browser's menu and choose Downloads.
  • iPhone and iPad: Safari saves downloads in the Files app, in the Downloads folder (on iCloud Drive or On My iPhone, depending on your settings).
  • Windows and Mac: in your Downloads folder, unless your browser asks where to save each file.

To edit it on a phone, open the .docx with the Microsoft Word, Google Docs or Pages app.

How do I convert a PDF I received on WhatsApp or by email?

First save the PDF to your phone or computer, then upload it to the converter. In WhatsApp, open the PDF and use the share or menu button to save it to Files (iPhone) or your Downloads (Android). In an email app, open the attachment and save it the same way. In the converter, tap "Choose PDF file" and pick it from that folder.

Microsoft Word, Google Docs and other apps

Can Microsoft Word open and convert a PDF?

Yes. Microsoft documents this for Word for Microsoft 365 and Word 2024, 2021, 2019 and 2016. When you open a PDF in Word, Word makes an editable copy and tries to match the original layout; the PDF itself is not changed. Microsoft notes that this works well mainly for documents that are mostly text, that the result may not look exactly like the PDF, and that a page made mostly of charts or graphics may come through as a single image you can't edit (Microsoft Support). Microsoft's page doesn't cover scanned PDFs, so for scans use a tool with OCR. For the steps, see converting a PDF in Microsoft Word.

What does Google Docs keep when it converts a PDF?

Google Docs mostly recovers text. According to Google's help page, bold, italics, font size, font type and line breaks are likely to be kept, while lists, tables, columns, footnotes and endnotes are not likely to be detected. Google also asks for files of 2 MB or smaller, text at least 10 pixels high and pages that are right side up (Google Drive Help). It is a reasonable free way to get the words out of a short document; for layout and tables, a dedicated converter usually does more.

ChatGPT and AI tools

Can ChatGPT or another AI tool convert a PDF to Word?

Partly, and it is worth knowing which part. Depending on the product and plan, AI assistants can read the text of a PDF you upload, summarize or rewrite it, and give you text, or sometimes a new document file, to use in Word. That is different from conversion:

  • Text extraction gets the words out. AI tools can do this, but long files may be shortened or paraphrased unless you ask for the exact text, so compare the result with the original.
  • Layout-preserving conversion rebuilds pages, tables, pictures and page order in a .docx. That is the job of a PDF to Word converter.
  • Reading scans depends on whether the AI tool can read images in the file; results vary.

Should I use an AI assistant or a PDF to Word converter?

Use a converter when you need the same document in an editable form: a contract, a form, a CV or a report you will update. Use an AI assistant when you want something new from the content, such as a summary, a translation or a rewritten version. In both cases, read the result before you rely on it, and check the tool's privacy terms before uploading confidential documents.

Privacy, safety and sending documents

Is it safe to convert a PDF to Word online?

It can be, if you choose the service with care. Before uploading, check:

  • that the site uses HTTPS (the padlock in the address bar);
  • that its privacy policy says how long uploaded and converted files are kept, and who can see them;
  • who runs the service and how to contact them.

For highly confidential documents, follow your employer's or client's rules, which may require an offline tool. On PDF2Wordly, files travel over an encrypted connection, are never made public, and are deleted after conversion and download, within 1 hour at most; nobody at PDF2Wordly reviews your files. The details are in our privacy policy.

Can I convert a PDF to Word without uploading it?

Not with an online converter: to convert your file, an online service, ours included, has to receive it on its server. To keep the file on your own computer, use desktop software that converts locally, such as Microsoft Word opening the PDF on your computer.

Should I send a document as PDF or Word?

Send a PDF when the other person should read, print or sign it exactly as you made it: final contracts, invoices, applications. Send a Word file when they need to edit it, add comments or track changes. If in doubt, follow the instructions you were given. For job applications specifically, see PDF or Word for your resume.
